papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Sensitive Component of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile framework for transferring behavior and representations from large teacher models to smaller student models. When applied with appropriate objectives, layer mappings, data strategies, and safeguards, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and communication while preserving much of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks. However, KD’s success is context-dependent: it interacts with teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, distribution shift, and fairness concerns. Treating KD as a configurable core of a compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, curriculum strategies, and privacy-aware protocols—yields the most reliable deployment outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Mechanisms, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically effective family of techniques that transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or auxiliary models into smaller, deployable students. KD supports many transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and training protocols (offline teacher, online mutual learning, self-distillation, multi-teacher and teacher-free schemes) and can be integrated with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. When carefully designed, KD not only approximates teacher performance but can act as a regularizer that improves generalization; however, reliable outcomes require attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data selection, layer alignment, and privacy or domain constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger or more complex teacher models into smaller, faster student models to meet constraints of latency, memory, privacy, or deployment. The field presents a diverse toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure), protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free), and architecture-aware adaptations that are frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, graphs, recommendation, and control shows distilled students can recover much teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and data strategies are addressed; however, KD faces limits from teacher–student mismatch, limited or absent data, propagation of teacher artifacts, and challenges in reliably transferring robustness, low-frequency behaviors, and fairness. Best practice treats KD as a toolbox within an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline, selecting distilled signals and data strategies according to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and highly practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD techniques range from simple soft-target matching to representation- and task-aware objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-augmentation and data-free protocols, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is effective across modalities and tasks but is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and augmentation, architecture alignment, and explicit handling of biases and distribution shift. Treated as a core component within an integrated compression pipeline and designed with task constraints in mind, KD yields reliable tradeoffs between efficiency and fidelity for deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: What is known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression strategies form a broad, practically driven toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or specialized teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students. Across modalities and tasks—classification, generation, retrieval, graph learning, self-supervision, and reinforcement learning—research has developed many algorithmic variants (logit and feature matching, attention/relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes), system-level protocols (federated, black-box, data-free), and architecture-aware methods (task-adaptive compression, neural architecture search, pruning and quantization combinations). Empirically, KD often substantially reduces latency and parameter counts while preserving a large fraction of teacher performance, but its success depends on teacher–student alignment, available data and augmentations, and task-specific design; remaining challenges include teacher bias transfer, degradation on low-frequency phenomena, domain shift, and heterogeneous-device constraints. Practical deployments balance distilled signals, data strategies, and architecture choices to achieve required trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, privacy, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Necessary but Not Sufficient Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and flexible framework for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers across vision, language, multimodal, and distributed settings. KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its effectiveness depends on choices about what is distilled, how teacher and student are aligned, and how distillation is combined with complementary compression techniques. Practical success therefore requires integrating KD with task-aware engineering—data strategies, multi-objective compression (pruning/quantization/architecture search), teacher/student co-design, and privacy-aware protocols—to avoid known failure modes and meet real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a narrow training trick into a broad, practical paradigm for compressing and adapting large deep models to resource- and data-constrained deployment settings. A rich family of KD formulations — from logit matching and feature imitation to adversarial, data-free, and online schemes — together with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and teacher ensembles) enables substantial reductions in memory and latency while largely preserving model quality. However, KD is not universally effective out-of-the-box: its benefits and risks depend on task characteristics, data availability, teacher–student compatibility, and deliberate choices of what and how to transfer. When practitioners treat KD as a toolkit of targeted strategies and validate choices against task constraints, it yields the best trade-offs between efficiency, robustness, and fidelity to the original model.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: The Case for Pragmatic, Task-Aware Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated set of techniques for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers. Across vision, language, multimodal, and distributed settings, distillation can preserve or even improve accuracy while enabling deployments with constrained compute, memory, latency, and privacy requirements. However, its success depends on matching distillation objectives and procedures to task constraints (e.g., robustness, heterogeneity, data availability). When applied thoughtfully—using feature-based objectives, ensemble or adversarial strategies, data augmentation or data-free approaches, and task-adaptive compression—KD reliably delivers practical trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Context‑Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and widely applicable approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Empirical and methodological work shows KD enables practical deployment across modalities and constrained settings, but its success depends on careful design choices, complementary compression primitives, and explicit safeguards against transferred errors and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers across vision, language, and multimodal settings. It can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints, and it interacts naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, distillation's success depends on the distillation objective, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and task-specific considerations; when these are not addressed it can propagate teacher errors, struggle with rare outputs, or fail due to optimization issues. Best practice is to treat KD as a configurable component of compression pipelines—combining logits, intermediate feature matching, projector modules, multi-teacher or teacher-adaptive designs, and data-aware schedules—to maximize student utility in real-world deployments.

papers_seen.author: Fernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Conditional, and Best-Practice Driven
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of techniques for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers. KD can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints, but its success is conditional on choices about what to transfer, the data used for distillation, teacher–student alignment, and complementary compression methods. Treating KD as a configurable component of compression pipelines — combining logits and feature objectives, projector modules, multi‑teacher or teacher‑adaptive designs, and data‑aware schedules — yields the most reliable results in real deployments.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: An Indispensable but Context‑Dependent Toolbox
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When matched to task constraints, data regimes, and student capacity, KD reliably produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, KD transfers teacher imperfections and faces limits (data mismatch, capacity gaps, low-frequency behavior), so it must be applied as a principled, task-aware set of techniques combined with complementary compression practices.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis from Recent Work
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Empirical results across vision, language, recommendation, multimodal, and generative domains show KD frequently preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication costs. Practical deployment favors combining KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), choosing appropriate transfer targets (logits, features, attention, decision-boundary signals), and adopting data- and task-aware strategies. KD also has well-documented limitations — optimization obstacles that prevent perfect teacher matching, sensitivity to teacher quality and data regimes, and risks of propagating teacher biases or poor modeling of rare phenomena — which motivate targeted mitigations such as adversarial/sample-selection methods, multi-teacher and teacher-aware schemes, data-free or privacy-preserving formulations, and representation-level objectives. Overall, KD is best viewed as a flexible, task-aware toolkit whose effectiveness depends on matching methods and safeguards to the compression and deployment goals.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Findings, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. A broad and practical toolbox has been developed—output-level (soft-target) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, contrastive and relational objectives, adversarial and data-free methods, online and multi-teacher protocols, and curriculum- or architecture-aware pipelines. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often recover most teacher performance and can improve generalization when objectives, layer mappings, and data choices are well matched to student capacity and task constraints. Success requires careful design around what to transfer, how to align layers and inputs, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate bias, rare-token degradation, and teacher errors; combining KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and neural architecture search) and using task-aware curricula or projectors typically yields better accuracy–efficiency trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Across domains and tasks—language modeling and translation, recommendation, graph learning, vision, continual and domain adaptation, and resource-constrained deployment—KD enables trade-offs between accuracy, latency, memory, privacy, and train-time complexity. Variants such as feature mimicking, self- and teacher-free distillation, ensemble and online distillation, data-free and privacy-aware schemes, and task- or domain-aware adaptations extend KD’s applicability. At the same time, careful choice of training targets, treatment of low-frequency phenomena, and consideration of the teacher-student mismatch are necessary to avoid transferring teacher errors and to realize the full benefits of distillation.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically driven framework for transferring predictive and representational information from large or composite teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. The literature shows a broad set of distillation objectives (soft logits, intermediate feature matching, attention and relational transfer, contrastive and adversarial schemes), multiple training protocols (multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free and synthetic-data approaches), and tight integration with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance in many settings, enable cross-modal and domain adaptation, and produce dramatic runtime and memory gains when applied with task-aware choices of signals, data, and student architectures. Important failure modes remain—teacher error propagation, capacity mismatch, data availability and heterogeneity, and fairness/privacy concerns—so best practice treats KD as a configurable toolbox that must be tailored to the task, data regime, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression: Evidence, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. KD has been shown to work across modalities and tasks by transferring logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structure. It can also be combined with data augmentation, adversarial schemes, online or teacher-free training, and architecture-aware adaptations to meet deployment constraints. KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on choices about which teacher signals to transfer, alignment of inputs and architectures, student capacity, and the availability or synthesis of suitable data. When used as part of a task-aware compression pipeline that addresses these issues, KD delivers substantial practical benefits for latency- and resource-constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches and Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile family of techniques for producing smaller, faster, or otherwise specialized models by transferring information from larger or alternative teacher models. KD variants include offline teacher-student distillation, online mutual distillation, ensemble-to-student distillation, cross-task distillation, and teacher-aware or student-aware training. Beyond the canonical logit-matching objective, modern work distills intermediate representations, relational and contrastive structures, and task-specific signals to improve accuracy, robustness, fairness, privacy, generation, and inference latency. Empirical results across computer vision, speech, machine translation, retrieval, graph learning, and routing problems show KD can both compress models without large accuracy loss and improve distilled students in multiple dimensions (robustness, fairness, generalization, and deployment cost). However, distillation is not a panacea: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality and compatibility, the choice of distilled knowledge (logits vs features vs relations), data complexity, and careful training strategies (sample selection, curriculum, annealing, or joint teacher-student learning). This synthesis summarizes methods, motivations, practical techniques, and empirical patterns observed across recent studies.

papers_seen.author: Hancock
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and transfers information from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. A wide family of distillation objectives and workflows—ranging from soft-logit matching to representation, relational, contrastive, adversarial, online, and meta-learned schemes—has been developed and applied across domains including vision, speech, graph learning, machine translation, and NLP. Empirical results show distillation often preserves most teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but success depends on careful design choices around teacher quality, student capacity, data, and objectives.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, faster, and more deployable models. Across vision, language, multimodal, graph, and federative settings, distillation can preserve much of a teacher's predictive quality while reducing inference latency, memory footprint, and communication costs. Different distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, contrastive signals) and training protocols (offline teacher→student, online/mutual, multi-teacher, data-free/zero-shot) make KD adaptable to diverse deployment constraints. At the same time, distillation has well-documented failure modes—transfer of teacher biases, degradation on rare or low-frequency phenomena, sensitivity to data heterogeneity and teacher–student capacity mismatch—and practical success depends on task-aware design choices and often combining KD with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. The field thus treats KD as a multifaceted, application-driven set of methods whose best practice is to match signals, data, and student capacity to deployment needs while applying targeted mitigations for privacy, robustness, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods provide practical routes to deploy high-performing deep models under resource, privacy, and latency constraints. The literature has developed diverse approaches that transfer information via soft logits, intermediate features, attentional maps, channel-wise statistics, and online mutual learning; adaptations address task-specific compression, data-free or few-shot regimes, large-scale distributed training, and teacher-student co-optimization. Empirical and theoretical analyses highlight that distillation combines information transfer with regularization effects, and that selecting what, when, and how to transfer knowledge (e.g., logits vs. features, offline vs. online, task-aware filtering) is crucial to achieve favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are no longer just ways to reduce parameter counts; when designed thoughtfully they preserve or even improve task performance, domain robustness, and privacy while enabling real-time deployment. Effective distillation requires going beyond matching output probabilities: transferring internal representations, using task- and domain-aware selection of teacher signals, leveraging ensemble or adversarial schemes when appropriate, and adopting data-aware or data-free augmentation techniques. In application domains from NLP to vision, multi-modal systems, and graph learning, tailored distillation strategies yield substantial speedups and parameter reductions with minimal loss (and sometimes gains) in accuracy. This paper synthesizes evidence across diverse recent works to advocate a principled, task-centered approach to distillation and compression.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable models while retaining much of teacher performance. The literature shows a wide range of KD mechanisms (logit- and feature-based losses, adversarial and data-free schemes, multi-teacher and online protocols) and application domains (NLP, vision, multimodal, detection, federated settings). KD succeeds best when combined with complementary practices—pretraining, layer-wise alignment, data augmentation, teacher adaptation, and hardware-aware compression—but it faces limitations from teacher errors, data absence, distributional mismatch, and heterogeneous deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations from teacher to student. A broad family of distillation techniques has been developed—logit (soft-label) matching, feature and layer-wise mimicry, multi-teacher and confidence-weighted schemes, adversarial and contrastive objectives, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants—enabling deployment across vision, language, graphs, recommender systems, and federated settings. While distillation often preserves most teacher performance and can even improve student generalization, effectiveness depends on what is transferred, layer alignment, teacher quality, availability and match of data, and complementary compression methods. This synthesis summarizes the operational variants, key empirical findings, domain-specific applications, common failure modes, and practical recommendations distilled from the provided studies.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central for deploying large deep models in latency- and resource-constrained settings. Across modalities and tasks, a consistent pattern is that distilled students can recover much of teacher performance when distillation addresses mismatches in architecture, data distribution, and input representations. Practical advances include multi-teacher and ensemble distillation, online and distributed distillation, data-free and zero-shot approaches, layer-wise and many-to-many layer mappings, task-aware selection of distilled information, and distillation formulations tailored to domain adaptation and federated settings. Theoretical and empirical analyses point to KD acting both as knowledge transfer and as a form of regularization; performance depends strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data augmentation, and instance-level selection of teacher signals. Remaining challenges include robust distillation under data heterogeneity, principled teacher selection, and aligning intermediate representations across heterogeneous detectors or modalities.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Transfer in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique that compresses large models into smaller, faster models while preserving or even improving task performance. Beyond simple size reduction, KD enables domain adaptation, multimodal capability lifting, robustness transfer, privacy-aware compression, and practical deployment on constrained hardware. The technique is complementary to pruning and quantization and can be adapted to settings with limited or no original training data, few-shot samples, and heterogeneous teacher ensembles. However, realizing KD's benefits reliably requires attention to teacher quality, sample selection, layer-mapping strategies, and interactions with regularization techniques such as label smoothing.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Patterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task‑aware Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practical framework for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of teacher performance. Across speech, vision, translation, and evaluation metrics, KD variants (soft labels, feature/attention matching, adversarial and data-free schemes, and self‑distillation) have enabled deployable models under latency, memory, privacy, and communication constraints. KD is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher errors, struggle with distribution or capacity mismatch, and require task‑aware adaptations. When used as part of an integrated, task‑aware compression pipeline—combining layer‑wise alignment, pretraining, pruning/quantization, data augmentation, or synthetic data generation—KD reliably yields practical tradeoffs between efficiency and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while enabling adaptation across tasks, domains, and modalities. When combined with representation-level objectives, careful teacher engineering, pre-training of compact architectures, and input-side interventions (e.g., augmentation or data synthesis), KD routinely yields large efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss and can enable deployment under tight compute, latency, or privacy constraints. At the same time, KD is not a single recipe: success depends on optimization choices, teacher–student alignment, and dataset properties, which motivates tailored distillation objectives, data strategies, and evaluation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Long
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse set of techniques has emerged — from soft-label/logit transfer to feature- and layer-level matching, adversarial or ensemble-driven schemes, data-free generation, and task-adaptive architecture search — yielding practical gains across NLP, vision, speech, and recommendation systems. Successes are widespread, but effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and careful alignment of objectives; combining KD with complementary compression methods and task-aware design is generally required for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster, and often more robust models across computer vision, NLP, multilingual metrics, and multimodal tasks. A range of complementary techniques — layer-wise mapping, data-free and zero-shot synthesis, self-distillation, adversarial and robust distillation, online/ensemble methods, and task-adaptive architecture search — together make distillation applicable under constraints such as limited data, privacy restrictions, heterogeneous devices, and production-scale training. I argue that adopting a portfolio of distillation strategies, chosen to match data availability and deployment constraints, yields the best trade-offs between efficiency, accuracy, robustness, and interpretability for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more expensive models (teachers) to smaller, cheaper models (students) to reduce inference cost, enable deployment on constrained devices, and support privacy- or resource-constrained settings. Approaches span soft-label distillation, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, data-free and zero-shot methods, multi-teacher and ensemble distillation, self-distillation, task- and modality-specific objectives, and combinations with pruning. Empirical work across vision, speech, 3D detection, recommender systems, and multiple NLP tasks demonstrates that carefully designed distillation strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while significantly reducing latency and memory. The literature also provides growing theoretical insight into when and how distillation helps, and identifies open challenges including imperfect teachers, domain shift, low-frequency token fidelity, modality mismatch, and heterogeneous-device federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a foundational technique for compressing large models into efficient, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD is effective across modalities (graphs, vision, speech, and NLP), supports privacy- and communication-constrained settings, can work without original training data, and admits algorithmic and theoretical refinements that improve robustness, interpretability, and efficiency. Combining representation-level objectives, adversarial or data-free sample generation, and task-aware layer mapping yields practical recipes for real-world compression and adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical strategy for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable students across modalities and tasks. KD techniques extend beyond matching logits: they include internal-representation distillation, adversarial and relational approaches, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware methods, and architecture-aware replacements. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can preserve or even improve generalization, enable domain adaptation, and permit deployment under resource, privacy, or latency constraints—provided practitioners attend to known failure modes such as teacher bias, low-frequency lexical errors, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Empirical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical toolkit for compressing large models into smaller, more efficient students while preserving predictive behavior and, in many cases, improving deployment properties such as latency, memory use, privacy, and robustness. The field has expanded from matching teacher logits to a broad set of signals and workflows — internal feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial and data-free generation, curriculum and selective-sample protocols, meta- and online-teaching schemes, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows that what to transfer (outputs vs. intermediate representations), how to align teacher and student (layer mapping, projectors), and which data to use (authentic, distilled, augmented, or synthetic) materially affect student outcomes. Practical deployments require task-aware design: align signals to student capacity, mitigate teacher error propagation, handle low-resource or privacy-constrained settings, and combine KD with complementary compression techniques. Remaining challenges include principled theory for which teacher signals are most informative across tasks, reliable transfer under data heterogeneity and domain shift, and preserving rare or structured outputs in sequence tasks.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is now a central, broadly applicable approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance and functional behavior of larger teachers. The literature describes a rich taxonomy of KD objectives and protocols — from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate features, attention maps, and relational or contrastive structures — together with specialized strategies for online, multi-teacher, data-free, federated, and privacy-sensitive settings. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often improves student generalization and acts as a regularizer, but success depends on task-aware choices: which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate transfer of teacher errors or low-frequency behaviors. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable component combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), curriculum and augmentation strategies, and targeted safeguards for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable method for transferring functionality from large teacher models to smaller students so that compressed models retain much of the teacher's performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and communication. KD covers a spectrum of techniques—from soft-target matching to internal representation transfer, multi-teacher/online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware approaches, and architecture-aware solutions such as task-adaptive compression—and integrates naturally with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, adversarial training). When implemented with care about teacher selection, data selection or synthesis, and representation alignment, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models across modalities; when misapplied it can propagate teacher errors, amplify biases, or fail due to optimization and data-mismatch issues. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a first-order engineering primitive for model compression in deep learning and NLP, and outlines recommended practices and known limitations to guide responsible adoption.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable students. Across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings, KD variants—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, and using data-free or adversarial generation—enable trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. Empirical and analytical work shows KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance, sometimes improve generalization, and enable deployment under privacy or resource constraints, while remaining sensitive to teacher quality, data availability, and teacher–student alignment.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Versatile Toolkit with Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a broad set of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, and sometimes more interpretable students. Across NLP and vision applications, KD enables deployment on resource-constrained hardware, supports privacy- and data-constrained settings, and can be adapted to preserve or transfer properties such as adversarial robustness, cross-modal behavior, and domain expertise. At the same time, KD interacts with factors such as teacher quality, data availability, label design, and training cost, and several specialized methods have been developed to address these practical trade-offs. This paper argues that KD is an indispensable, flexible approach for model compression and adaptation, and that best results arise from combining KD with complementary practices (e.g., pre-training, augmentation, curriculum selection, or generative replay) tailored to the deployment constraints and objectives.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are widely used to transfer behavior from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. Work across vision, generative modeling, reinforcement learning, recommendation, and language has developed diverse objectives and mechanisms — soft-label matching, internal-representation matching, adversarial synthesis of training data, multi-teacher/ensemble supervision, layer-wise and task-adaptive compression, and data-augmentation-enhanced distillation. These approaches trade off accuracy, inference cost, and robustness and address practical constraints such as lack of access to original training data, domain shift, fairness, and heterogeneous model architectures. Empirical results show distilled students can approach or sometimes match teacher performance while substantially reducing FLOPs, parameters, or latency, but limitations remain in data heterogeneity, low-frequency token transfer, and privacy-constrained settings. This synthesis summarizes methods, empirical findings, applications, and open challenges documented in the provided literature.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or adapts large or multi-modal models into smaller, faster, or specialized students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, generative models, and domain- or privacy-constrained settings, a diverse toolbox has been developed—soft-label supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, multi- and ensemble-teacher schemes, self- and online-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and architecture-aware adaptations (e.g., pruning, layer skipping, NAS). Empirical results show that appropriately designed KD pipelines can produce compact models that approach teacher performance and enable deployment in resource-constrained environments, while practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, and optimization design. Remaining challenges include principled theory linking teacher signals to student generalization, reliable distillation under heterogeneous architectures or non-iid data, privacy-and-fairness-aware protocols, and extending KD to complex generative and structured prediction tasks.
