papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods transfer predictive behavior or internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce memory, compute, and latency while retaining much of task performance. Methods span soft-target (logit) matching, representation- and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and ensemble guidance, online and adversarial schemes, and data-free/zero-shot approaches. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a mechanism for knowledge transfer and as an implicit regularizer, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and the particular distillation objective. Practical deployments combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet resource, privacy, and latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger, more expensive models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The literature has expanded from simple logit-matching to a diverse toolbox that includes intermediate-feature matching, attention and relational objectives, self- and multi-teacher schemes, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and hybrid pipelines that combine pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware search. Empirical work shows that with task-aware objectives and careful handling of teacher-student mismatches, distilled students can approach teacher performance across vision and language tasks, though important challenges remain around data scarcity, teacher imperfection, capacity mismatch, and reliably distilling structured or generative outputs.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Evidence, Methods, and Open Problems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practically validated set of techniques for transferring information from high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students so they can be deployed under latency, memory, compute, and privacy constraints. A broad toolkit—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi- and self-distillation, data-free or privacy-aware synthesis, and curriculum or adversarial sample selection—enables students to retain much of teacher performance across vision, language, multimodal, retrieval, and federated settings. Despite strong empirical successes, important engineering and scientific challenges remain around teacher–student alignment, data availability and synthesis, preservation of low-frequency behaviors, robustness and fairness, and principled automated design for heterogeneous deployment environments.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used framework for transferring predictive behavior from large, expensive teachers to smaller, efficient students. Across vision, language, recommendation, graph, and multimodal tasks, KD has been extended beyond logits-matching into feature and layer-level mimicry, online and self-distillation, adversarial and contrastive objectives, task-adaptive architecture search, and combinations with pruning and quantization. Empirical results show KD enables substantial latency and memory reductions while often preserving accuracy, improving calibration, and helping robustness; success depends strongly on choices about what to transfer, teacher quality, data and augmentation, and alignment strategies between heterogeneous models.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical technique for producing compact, efficient models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models to smaller students. KD methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals, synthetic data) and in protocol (offline, online, self-distillation, many-to-many layer mapping, data-free variants). Empirical results across vision, language, generation, and graph domains demonstrate that distilled students can approach teacher performance when distillation is carefully designed and combined with complementary compression techniques; however, success depends on factors such as teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and explicit mitigation of failure modes including bias transfer and degraded performance on rare phenomena. Best practice treats KD as a configurable component of a broader compression pipeline that also uses pretraining, architecture-aware design, and safeguards for privacy and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and practically essential approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, or specialized models. When designed around task constraints, student capacity, and available data, KD preserves much of a teacher's capabilities while enabling deployment under compute, memory, latency, and privacy limits. Its greatest value comes from treating distillation as a configurable toolkit—combining soft-targets, representation matching, adversarial or data-free sample synthesis, and multi-teacher or self-distillation—with complementary compression techniques to meet real-world constraints. Success requires careful handling of teacher–student alignment, data scarcity, distribution shift, and bias transfer, but a task-aware, hybrid pipeline makes KD one of the most practical routes to effective model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and widely applicable approach for producing smaller, faster, and often more deployable models by transferring information from larger or specialized models. It supports a broad range of objectives beyond raw compression—improving robustness, enabling domain adaptation, supporting privacy-aware or federated workflows, and permitting deployment on constrained hardware. KD methods range from simple soft-label matching to richer transfers of intermediate representations, attention patterns, and relational or contrastive structure. While KD frequently yields strong empirical gains, its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, alignment between teacher and student, data availability and distribution, and the choice of signals and losses. When applied with attention to these constraints and combined sensibly with other compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design), KD is a practical foundational technique for real-world model compression in vision, language, and multimodal systems.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Insights, and Applications (Synthesis)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A broad toolkit has emerged — including logits/soft-label transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, adversarial and contrastive objectives, online and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search — enabling deployment across vision, speech, language, generative, and multimodal settings. Empirical and theoretical work highlights gains in latency, memory, calibration, and sometimes robustness, while pointing to failure modes driven by teacher quality, capacity mismatch, data scarcity, and distribution shift; best practice treats KD as a core element of a broader, context-aware compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models using targets ranging from soft logits to intermediate representations and relational signals. Across vision, language, multimodal, and speech tasks, KD combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data augmentation or synthetic-data generation) enables deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain constraints. Empirical results show distilled students often recover most teacher performance and can sometimes match or exceed teachers when distillation is carefully designed. Important open problems include teacher–student capacity mismatch, optimization and belief-matching limits, distribution shift and domain adaptation, preserving rare-token/low-frequency behavior, and avoiding transfer of teacher biases. This synthesis summarizes mechanisms, practical variants, representative empirical patterns, and recommended directions for research and deployment.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression, Transfer, and Robustification in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a technique for shrinking models: it is a flexible paradigm that enables model compression, domain and modality transfer, continual adaptation, and improved interpretability and fairness. A range of strategies — from many-to-many layer alignment and feature mimicking to data-free synthesis, online peer teaching, and augmentation-aware distillation — make KD applicable across tasks (classification, generation, detection, ASR, GANs) and settings (distributed training, privacy-constrained, few-shot, multi-task). However, practical use requires careful design choices (what to transfer, how to match teacher and student, and how to handle teacher–student discrepancy and label-processing artifacts). When applied with methods matched to these considerations, KD consistently yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance while unlocking deployment and research scenarios otherwise infeasible for large, monolithic networks.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Castaneda
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Toolbox for Model Compression: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster, or specialized students. Empirical and theoretical work across vision, language, graph, and generative domains shows KD can substantially reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but its success depends on choices about transfer targets, data availability, teacher quality, and complementary compression methods. Treating KD as a principled toolbox—combining logits, feature- and relation-level objectives, data strategies, and hardware-aware techniques—yields the most reliable route to practical, robust compression.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under compute, memory, latency, privacy, or domain constraints. A diverse toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational structure, and decision-boundary or synthetic-data signals), training protocols (single/multi-teacher, online/self-distillation, task- and layer-aware schedules), and architecture-aware adaptations (projectors, layer mapping, and combinations with pruning/quantization/NAS) has been developed. Empirically, properly designed distillation pipelines recover a large fraction of teacher performance across vision, language, multimodal, and generative tasks, and can be combined with complementary compression methods to meet device and domain requirements. Remaining challenges include optimization gaps, teacher–student capacity mismatch, distribution shift and data scarcity (including privacy- and data-free regimes), and trade-offs among accuracy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible framework for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. Across vision, language, graph, and generative modeling, KD methods vary by what is transferred (teacher logits, internal representations, attention, relational structure), how layers are aligned or projected, and how data constraints (limited access, privacy, or distribution shift) are handled. Empirical work demonstrates that combining output-level and representation-level objectives, using layer-mapping or projector modules, and adapting training data or curricula yields the best trade-offs between compactness and accuracy. Despite wide success, effective distillation requires careful choices about teacher quality, distilled signals, sample selection, and safeguards for robustness, privacy, and low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: The Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster, or more interpretable students across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains. KD can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and progressive replacement to yield compact models that preserve much of teacher performance, but its effectiveness depends on dataset complexity, teacher quality, and the choice of what and how to transfer. Addressing pitfalls such as harmful teacher supervision on particular samples, degraded signals for low-frequency outputs, data unavailability, privacy concerns, and fairness requires targeted strategies (selective distillation, adapted teachers, self-distillation, generative replay, or tailored objectives).

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger or more complex teacher models into smaller, faster student models to meet constraints of latency, memory, privacy, or deployment. The field presents a diverse toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure), protocols (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, data-free), and architecture-aware adaptations that are frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical work across vision, language, graphs, recommendation, and control shows distilled students can recover much teacher performance when teacher quality, student capacity, and data strategies are addressed; however, KD faces limits from teacher–student mismatch, limited or absent data, propagation of teacher artifacts, and challenges in reliably transferring robustness, low-frequency behaviors, and fairness. Best practice treats KD as a toolbox within an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline, selecting distilled signals and data strategies according to deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, often over-parameterized teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. Over the past decade these techniques have diversified from simple logit-matching to a broad set of objectives and pipelines — including feature- and representation-matching, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial procedures, data-free and privacy-aware methods, multi-teacher schemes, teacher design, and selective sample strategies. KD has been applied across domains (NLP, vision, graph learning, generative models, novel-view synthesis, speech, and recommender systems), producing substantial reductions in parameters and latency while retaining or sometimes improving downstream performance. The literature highlights important practical trade-offs (utility vs. fairness, robustness, data availability, and teacher–student mismatch), and suggests promising directions in adaptive teacher design, rigorous uncertainty and fairness controls, and domain- and task-specific distillation objectives.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, Strengths, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core set of techniques for transferring information from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models. Through objectives that match outputs, internal representations, or relational structure, KD enables reductions in latency, memory, and compute while often retaining much of teacher performance. The approach has been extended into many variants—feature- and layer-level alignment, attention- or projector-based mappings, multi-teacher and online schemes, data‑free and privacy-aware protocols, curriculum and adversarial sample strategies—and is applied across classification, retrieval, translation, evaluation metrics, and graph learning. Practical deployment requires addressing optimization and capacity mismatches, data and distributional constraints, and potential transfer of teacher artifacts; combining KD with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware distillation design produces the best results. Open directions center on principled selection of what to distill, robust distillation under data heterogeneity or privacy constraints, and automated, deployment-aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, retrieval, generative modeling, and federated settings. A broad set of techniques—matching soft logits, imitating intermediate features or attention, adversarial and curriculum-based sample selection, ensemble and multi-teacher guidance, and data- or privacy-aware generation—enable students to retain much of teacher performance while reducing parameters, latency, and memory. Empirical evidence shows distilled students often approach teacher performance, but limitations persist (teacher errors, optimization gaps, domain and data mismatch, low-frequency phenomena, and heterogeneity of devices/architectures). Advances such as feature-based distillation, curriculum strategies, adversarial sample use, many-to-many layer alignment, student-friendly teacher design, and teacher-free/self-distillation extend applicability and mitigate failure modes. Key open problems include principled theory for which teacher signals matter across tasks, robust private and data-free distillation, and automated co-design of student architectures and distillation objectives for heterogeneous deployments.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a heuristic for compressing neural networks into a broad, practically validated family of techniques for producing compact models that retain much of the functionality of larger teachers. KD methods transfer information via outputs, intermediate features, relational signals, or synthesized data, and they are applied across modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs, multimodal) and problem classes (classification, detection, generation, reinforcement learning, segmentation, view synthesis). Practical success depends on matching the distillation strategy to the task and deployment constraints (data availability, privacy, capacity, latency, hardware), and on integrating KD with complementary compression methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware adaptations. Remaining challenges include teacher imperfections, capacity mismatch, limited or private data, and preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviour in sequence models.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer behavior or internal representations from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models to reduce latency, memory, and communication costs while retaining performance. Across modalities, researchers have developed logits-based supervision, feature and attention matching, many-to-many layer mapping, multi-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-constrained distillation, and architecture-aware compression. These methods are applied to enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, federated and privacy-sensitive settings, domain adaptation, generative-model compression, and improved fairness or robustness when combined with task-aware design. Despite strong empirical gains, important challenges remain in handling distribution shift, low-frequency phenomena, heterogeneous architectures, and data-scarce or data-free scenarios. Emerging directions emphasize student-aware teacher design, joint optimization with pruning and NAS, federated/distilled learning across heterogeneous devices, and cross-modal distillation for generative and segmentation tasks.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Practical Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision, language, speech, detection, recommendation, and multimodal tasks, KD methods—ranging from soft-logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, adversarial and contrastive objectives, data-free synthesis, and online or multi-teacher protocols—enable substantial efficiency gains while often preserving much of teacher performance. Success depends on choices about what to transfer, data strategy, teacher–student alignment, and complementary compression (e.g., pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Practical deployments use task-aware adaptations, confidence- or curriculum-based weighting, and privacy- or federated-aware designs; remaining challenges include teacher–student mismatch, limited or private data, distribution shift, rare-output transfer, and principled theory for optimal transfer.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible framework for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD encompasses a range of targets and protocols—output-level supervision, intermediate representation matching, adversarial and data-free synthesis, multi-teacher and self-distillation—and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques. While KD routinely delivers favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-offs in vision, language, recommender, and multimodal systems, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data availability and privacy, fairness and low-frequency behavior, and method selection for the deployment constraints at hand.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods form a broad, practical toolkit for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, efficient student models. Over the past decade KD variants—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to representation-level matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and data- or privacy-aware protocols—have been adapted to many tasks and modalities (vision, language, speech, multimodal, generative models, and federated settings). Empirical work shows KD frequently preserves most teacher performance while enabling large reductions in latency, memory, and parameter count; success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, data availability, and optimization. Remaining challenges include principled theory for when and what to transfer, reliable distillation across heterogeneous architectures and non‑i.i.d. data, mitigation of bias and teacher errors, and robust data-free or privacy-preserving protocols.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Work
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central approach for transferring behavior from large, expensive models (teachers) to smaller, more efficient models (students). Across modalities and tasks, KD is used both as a compression technique and as a means to inject inductive biases, stabilize continual learning, preserve privacy, and improve efficiency (compute, memory, latency) under deployment constraints. Practical KD pipelines combine logit-based supervision, intermediate-feature matching, architectural replacements, and training-time regularizers; they are often complemented with pruning, low-precision numerics, layer skipping, data augmentation, or specialized alignment strategies to handle mismatched inputs or modalities. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can capture “dark knowledge” beyond labels, transfer inductive biases, and sometimes enable students to outperform their teachers when paired with careful pre-training, data strategies, or architectural design. This synthesis summarizes techniques, motivations, and empirical patterns found in recent studies, and highlights open engineering considerations for applying KD in NLP, vision, graph, and multimodal systems.

papers_seen.author: Mccarthy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses and transfers knowledge from larger or more complex teacher models into smaller, efficient student models. A broad family of methods—soft-target (logit) transfer, intermediate-feature and attention matching, contrastive and relational objectives, and data-free or teacher-free variants—has been developed and successfully applied across vision, language, graphs, speech, and multimodal problems. Practical success depends on teacher design, data and curriculum choices, alignment of teacher and student representations, and combining KD with complementary compression tools.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Power, Limits, and Practical Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and widely applicable approach to compress large models into lightweight students for deployment across vision, speech, graph, and NLP tasks. KD variants transfer information via logits, intermediate features, or data synthesized from teachers; they can also be combined with privacy or fairness measures. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization difficulties, dataset mismatches, and design choices (what to mimic, which layers, how to align teacher and student) strongly affect outcomes. Careful method selection—feature vs. logit supervision, layer alignment, projector usage, sample selection, and teacher adaptation—enables consistent gains while meeting constraints like limited data, privacy, or fairness.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or adapts large or multi-modal models into smaller, faster, or specialized students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, generative models, and domain- or privacy-constrained settings, a diverse toolbox has been developed—soft-label supervision, intermediate feature and attention matching, multi- and ensemble-teacher schemes, self- and online-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and architecture-aware adaptations (e.g., pruning, layer skipping, NAS). Empirical results show that appropriately designed KD pipelines can produce compact models that approach teacher performance and enable deployment in resource-constrained environments, while practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability and selection, and optimization design. Remaining challenges include principled theory linking teacher signals to student generalization, reliable distillation under heterogeneous architectures or non-iid data, privacy-and-fairness-aware protocols, and extending KD to complex generative and structured prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Task-Aware Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically indispensable approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students across modalities. When designed with task-aware choices about which teacher signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student inputs and capacities, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD reliably yields major efficiency gains with modest performance loss. KD also enables deployment under privacy and communication constraints, and can transfer robustness when done adversarially, but it has well-documented failure modes—teacher bias, domain shift, degradation on low-frequency phenomena, and mismatches between teacher and student—that must be mitigated with targeted strategies such as multi-teacher schedules, sample selection, teacher adaptation, and privacy-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Conditional Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers across vision, language, and multimodal settings. It can recover much of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints, and it interacts naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, distillation's success depends on the distillation objective, teacher–student alignment, data strategy, and task-specific considerations; when these are not addressed it can propagate teacher errors, struggle with rare outputs, or fail due to optimization issues. Best practice is to treat KD as a configurable component of compression pipelines—combining logits, intermediate feature matching, projector modules, multi-teacher or teacher-adaptive designs, and data-aware schedules—to maximize student utility in real-world deployments.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used framework for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, efficient student models while retaining much of the original performance. A diverse family of distillation objectives and workflows—ranging from soft-label/logit matching to feature- and representation-level imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, adversarial schemes, multi-teacher and self-supervised variants—has been developed and adapted across modalities (vision, language, multimodal, graphs, and generative models). Empirical work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but outcomes depend strongly on choices of distillation targets, teacher quality and friendliness, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and task-specific adaptations. Open challenges include handling mismatches in capacity or data, preserving rare-token or long-tail behavior, and formalizing best practices for combining KD with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central tools for deploying high-performing deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Work in this area has progressed beyond the original formulation of training a small student to match a teacher's output probabilities: modern approaches distill internal representations, perform many-to-many layer alignment, operate without access to original training data, combine multiple teachers or ensembles, and adapt to particular architectures and tasks (including graph networks, detectors, generative models, and language models). Practical concerns such as data heterogeneity, privacy guarantees, and robustness to distribution shift have motivated methods that use synthetic data, private perturbations, generative replay, and federated or online distillation protocols. The field continues to trade off fidelity to teacher behavior, compactness, task specificity, and deployability, with task-adaptive compression and representation-alignment methods emerging as especially effective for NLP and other structured prediction tasks.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical paradigm for producing compact, efficient models by transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teacher models to smaller student models. A diverse set of distillation objectives and workflows — including soft-logit matching, intermediate representation and attention imitation, relational and contrastive objectives, multi- and self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware protocols, and adversarial or curriculum-based training — has been developed and applied across modalities (NLP, vision, speech, graphs) and tasks (classification, generation, detection, ranking, and more). When combined with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, KD routinely enables deployment in resource- and latency-constrained settings while often preserving most teacher performance. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher-student compatibility, data regimes, and mitigation of failure modes such as bias transfer, optimization mismatch, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a logits-matching trick into a broad, practical framework for shrinking and adapting large models while retaining much of their performance. Modern KD techniques include soft-target transfer, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and ensemble-teacher schemes, online and distributed formulations, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Across vision, language, recommendation, and domain-adaptation settings, KD is most effective when combined with complementary strategies (pretraining, pruning, quantization, curriculum or online training, and task-aware losses). Despite strong empirical successes, practitioners must attend to teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and domain mismatch; many current research directions focus on robust, privacy-preserving, and data-limited distillation for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Foundational, Versatile, but Imperfect Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable framework for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to meet deployment, privacy, and latency constraints. KD spans logits-based supervision, representation and feature matching, adversarial and generator-based data synthesis, multi-teacher or online schemes, and task- and domain-aware adaptations. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful training practices (projectors, curriculum, selective sampling), KD can recover much of teacher performance and enable new capabilities (cross-domain transfer, federated heterogeneity, and multi-modal compression). However, KD is not a turnkey solution: success depends on teacher–student compatibility, data availability (including data-free or few-shot regimes), distribution shift, and mitigation of propagated teacher errors or biases. Practitioners should treat KD as a flexible framework that must be adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: The Central Role of Knowledge Distillation for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and widely applicable approach to compressing models for deployment in resource-constrained settings. Distillation can transfer many types of knowledge (logits, intermediate features, attention patterns, relational or contrastive signals) and can be adapted to scenarios that lack original training data, require privacy guarantees, or demand task- and hardware-aware compression. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, architecture search, pretraining, or ensemble teaching), KD enables large reductions in model size and latency while largely preserving performance. Nevertheless, distillation can propagate biases and teacher artifacts and needs targeted remedies (feature-focused objectives, multi-teacher strategies, teacher annealing, or exposure to raw data) to avoid failure modes on rare phenomena. The literature demonstrates both the breadth of KD methods and concrete best practices to maximize effectiveness across vision, speech, graph, and NLP tasks.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Cross-Domain Argument for Practical, Responsible, and Multi-Modal Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques are indispensable for deploying modern deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Across vision, language, graph, and generative domains, distillation methods can preserve most of a teacher's performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication. Best results come from (a) matching appropriate internal representations (layer mapping, attention, many-to-many mappings), (b) designing teachers or multi-teacher schemes that are student-aware, and (c) combining distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, NAS, adversarial training, federated schemes). However, practitioners must be mindful of failure modes—bias amplification, degraded modeling of rare phenomena, and gaps when no training data are available—and adopt targeted mitigations such as task-adaptive compression, confidence-aware multi-teacher weighting, and data-free or privacy-preserving distillation when necessary.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring information from large, often multi-modal or ensemble teachers into smaller, faster student models to enable deployment under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. Across vision and language tasks KD has been adapted into many forms — soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention matching, relational and contrastive objectives, online and offline protocols, and data-free or zero-shot schemes — and is frequently combined with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can recover much of teacher performance in many settings when teacher quality, student capacity, and appropriate data or synthesis strategies are addressed; theoretical and empirical analyses highlight KD’s role both as knowledge transfer and as a regularizer. Despite broad success, KD faces limits from teacher–student mismatch, limited or heterogeneous data, and propagation of teacher artifacts; current best practice is to treat KD as one element of an integrated, task-aware compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Context-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and highly practical approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD techniques range from simple soft-target matching to representation- and task-aware objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-augmentation and data-free protocols, and integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is effective across modalities and tasks but is not a silver bullet: its success depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and augmentation, architecture alignment, and explicit handling of biases and distribution shift. Treated as a core component within an integrated compression pipeline and designed with task constraints in mind, KD yields reliable tradeoffs between efficiency and fidelity for deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Studies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical and flexible pathway to compress large neural models into smaller, faster students while preserving much of their performance. Across NLP and other modalities, researchers have developed logit-level, representation-level, layer-wise, multi-teacher, data-free, privacy-aware, and task-aware distillation variants and combined KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows that careful choice of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data and low-frequency phenomena materially affects student quality and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students while retaining much of their performance. KD encompasses logits-based, feature- and representation-level, multi-teacher, online, self-distillation, and privacy-aware variants, and its effectiveness depends on choosing what to transfer, matching student capacity to teacher signals, and integrating complementary compression and training practices. When combined with architecture-aware design, augmentation or synthetic-data generation, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols, KD enables deployable models across resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical, and Nuanced Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for producing compact, efficient models from larger or ensemble teachers. It supports a wide range of objectives—logit-level transfer, feature- and representation-level matching, relational and adversarial objectives, and many-to-many layer mappings—and is applicable across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models) and settings (offline, online, data-free, federated, multi-teacher). When combined with careful teacher-student co-design, targeted data strategies, and complementary compression techniques, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while also serving secondary goals such as interpretability or robustness. KD is powerful but not automatic: success depends on matching objectives to tasks, mitigating teacher-induced errors or biases, and addressing optimization and data-distribution challenges.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is now a central, broadly applicable approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance and functional behavior of larger teachers. The literature describes a rich taxonomy of KD objectives and protocols — from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate features, attention maps, and relational or contrastive structures — together with specialized strategies for online, multi-teacher, data-free, federated, and privacy-sensitive settings. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often improves student generalization and acts as a regularizer, but success depends on task-aware choices: which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate transfer of teacher errors or low-frequency behaviors. Practical pipelines therefore treat KD as a configurable component combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), curriculum and augmentation strategies, and targeted safeguards for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques form a broad, practical toolkit for transferring capabilities of large or ensemble models into smaller, faster, or more deployable models while retaining much of their task performance. Approaches span matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations, many-to-many layer mappings, attention- and projector-based transfers, data-free and zero-shot schemes, multi-teacher and online protocols, and integrations with quantization, pruning, and architecture search. Empirical work across language, vision, 3D perception, retrieval, and federated settings shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when distillation is combined with suitable data strategies, teacher design, and complementary compression methods. Important open challenges remain in data-scarce or privacy-sensitive regimes, robust transfer across heterogeneous architectures, and principled selection of what and how to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable method for transferring functionality from large teacher models to smaller students so that compressed models retain much of the teacher's performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and communication. KD covers a spectrum of techniques—from soft-target matching to internal representation transfer, multi-teacher/online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware approaches, and architecture-aware solutions such as task-adaptive compression—and integrates naturally with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, adversarial training). When implemented with care about teacher selection, data selection or synthesis, and representation alignment, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models across modalities; when misapplied it can propagate teacher errors, amplify biases, or fail due to optimization and data-mismatch issues. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a first-order engineering primitive for model compression in deep learning and NLP, and outlines recommended practices and known limitations to guide responsible adoption.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Demand-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, broadly applicable framework for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teachers' utility. KD methods span output matching, feature- and layer-level alignment, self- and ensemble-distillation, meta-learned and student-friendly teacher designs, and data- or task-aware adaptations. Empirical work across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks demonstrates KD’s ability to deliver large reductions in model size and compute with modest performance loss, and in many cases to improve robustness or generalization when combined with appropriate procedures. At the same time, KD’s reliability depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data; addressing these constraints through architectural design, curriculum and meta-learning, augmentation and synthetic-data strategies, and multi-teacher or online schemes is central to practical deployment.
